name: Students using ChatGPT to cheat on schoolwork
what_it_is: Comedy skits and talking-head clips about students using ChatGPT to do assignments and homework, and getting away with it or being caught. Videos include a student bragging about AI-ing a whole assignment for a good grade, a tutor confronting a student over AI-written homework, a talk-show clip joking about explaining work "clearly done by ChatGPT," and a South Park scene about students secretly using it for essays.

what_we_now_know: What is now known is that a second-grade teacher reports a student photographed his measurement homework and asked ChatGPT for the answers instead of using a ruler, an r/Professors thread diagnoses a pattern where students' AI-produced homework is perfect while their in-person midterm performance collapses, a teacher reports that 15 of 22 students who submitted a quarterly essay used AI, University of Illinois CS 374 course policy treats generative-AI chatbots as a permitted, citable source for homework as long as disclosed and independently worded and requires students to explain what they used an LLM for, and of 50 YouTube results for «students using ChatGPT to cheat on homework» of any length, uploaded in the last month, sorted by relevance, 6 are about this subject (12%), of 50 YouTube results for «students submitting AI-generated homework» 11 are about this subject (22%), and of 50 YouTube results for «teachers detecting AI written homework students» uploaded in the last year, 40 are about this subject (80%).
